name: Chat mode vs Agent mode
what: Two top-level modes: Chat mode gives instant answers (images, PDFs, text files, web search) and costs no credits; Agent mode plans and executes multi-step tasks in a sandbox and consumes credits.
how: Mode is per-task; '/chatmode' slash command switches to Chat mode. Since 2.0 Chat mode runs on third-party fast chat models (unnamed); Agent mode runs Manus 2.0 Lite/2.0/2.0 Max agent profiles.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's chat page needs an explicit cheap-chat vs metered-agent split with a visible cost boundary.
notes: Free chat mode is a strong acquisition lever; the credit boundary is explicit in docs.

name: Branch (session branching)
what: Hover any earlier message and click a branch icon to fork a parallel session that inherits instructions, files and history up to that point; original stays untouched; branches can be branched again; a 'Branched from' breadcrumb links back.
how: Server-side copy of context snapshot per branch (isolated copy, no cross-branch effects). Not supported in Web Builder sessions at launch (2026-07-09).
verevonRelevance: Maps directly onto Model Plane runs/sessions: a run-graph with parent pointer and context snapshot would give Verevon the same affordance.
notes: ChatGPT/Claude have edit-and-regenerate; Manus makes forks first-class and navigable.

name: Task References (@ past tasks)
what: Users (and API callers) can bring earlier tasks into a new chat; the agent browses them on demand (outline, search conversation and files, read parts) rather than injecting full content.
how: API: message.task_references (<=20 ids, 22-char ids, accumulate across sendMessage, oldest dropped beyond 20; access checked lazily at read time). Mobile: type @ to reference a past task (release notes 26.11.x).
verevonRelevance: Lazy, tool-driven cross-session retrieval (not RAG dump) is a good pattern for Verevon session search and Data Plane retrieval.
notes: Lazy access check and 'not found' tolerance are notable design choices.

name: Projects (persistent workspaces)
what: Projects hold a master instruction, knowledge-base files, skills, connectors and related sessions; new sessions inherit the configuration; sidebar groups sessions by project.
how: Instruction updates apply on the next message of existing sessions; file updates only to new sessions. API: project.create/list/detail/update (name, instructions, connectors, skills). Team projects: owner/editors set shared SOPs; invitees see only their own sessions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Spaces/projects should bind instructions + files + connectors + skills as one inheritable config object.
notes: Launched 2025-12-01.

name: Library of generated artifacts
what: A Library centralizes all generated files and outputs (websites, apps, games, documents, slides, spreadsheets, images, video, audio) with favorites and type filters.
how: artifact.list API: 10 mutually exclusive types classified by indexed file type; Website/WebDev/Slides precedence; cursor pagination with expiry; signed CDN URLs expire in 48h; slides exportable via task.listMessages slides_format=pptx, markdown_format=pdf|docx.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs an artifact index decoupled from chat transcripts, with typed classification and export formats.

name: Task sharing with public link and replay
what: A share control on each task creates a public link; recipients see the conversation and output artifacts (not the sandbox); team guests can watch task replays and comment.
how: share_visibility private|team|public on task.create/update; share_url returned. Guest role (free, unlimited) can view deliverables, replays, download, comment, but not prompt.
verevonRelevance: Replay-able shared runs plus a free viewer role is a cheap collaboration surface for Verevon.

name: Real-time collaboration (Collab) in a task
what: Owner invites up to 49 collaborators into one task; collaborators can instruct the agent and reach sandbox files through it; only the owner pays credits.
how: Share button > collaboration > invite. Connectors are automatically disabled when collaboration is on; sandbox login cookies are cleared when the first collaborator joins.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Application Plane realtime projections could host multi-user runs; note Manus' rule that personal connectors are disabled in shared runs (ACL never widens).
notes: Disabling connectors is a security decision aligned with Verevon's 'Space access never widens ACL'.

name: Message queueing during a running task
what: Users can queue multiple messages while the agent works; they are processed in order (each builds and deploys in WebDev with Auto-Publish).
how: Documented in Auto-Publish FAQ; the run loop drains queued user messages sequentially.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane run queue should accept steering messages mid-run.

name: Slash command menu in composer
what: Typing '/' opens a command menu: Plan, Skills (/SKILL_NAME), /chatmode, /manus-api; mobile uses '+' menu.
how: Composer command palette; skills are listed from the user's installed/Project skills.
verevonRelevance: Standard; Verevon composer should expose modes and skills via '/'.

name: Task list, hidden tasks and deletion recovery
what: Tasks appear in a task list; API tasks can be hidden from the list (hide_in_task_list) but remain reachable by URL; deleted tasks can be recovered (help article) and listed with include_deleted.
how: task.list include_deleted=true returns status 'deleted' with deleted_at; task.delete is permanent; help article covers recovery of deleted tasks.
verevonRelevance: Soft-delete with tombstones and a 'hidden from list' flag for programmatic runs.

name: Localized output language per task
what: Tasks can specify output locale (en, zh-CN, ja, ...); site has 10+ language variants of blog/docs.
how: task.create locale parameter; default is account locale.
verevonRelevance: Verevon (Norwegian-first) should carry locale on runs, not only on the UI.

name: Slides generation (Standard, Image, PowerPoint modes)
what: Slides tool with a mode dropdown: Standard (web deck), Image (Nano Banana Pro / GPT Image 2 image slides, editable), PowerPoint (native .pptx with data-backed charts, mergeable tables, slide masters).
how: Agent researches, outlines, then generates slide by slide; PPT mode outputs native pptx; chart toolbar with Elements and Edit Data (spreadsheet overlay). Inputs: topic, spreadsheets, Google Sheets via Workspace connector, PDFs, URLs, transcripts; Wide Research for multi-source.
verevonRelevance: Slides is a top Manus use case; Verevon should at minimum produce editable pptx with live chart data.
notes: PowerPoint mode Beta on 1.6/Max (2026-07-14). Editable image slides claimed as 'first' (2025-12-18).

name: Design View / Canvas (image creation and local editing)
what: Interactive canvas to generate images and make point-and-click local edits: Mark Tool selects regions with per-region instructions, in-image text extraction/editing, combine multiple images, batch edits; mobile press-and-hold marking with voice.
how: Powered by Google Nano Banana Pro; Canvas also hosts video models (Seedance 2.0/2.5, MiniMax H3, Veo 3.1 Standard).
verevonRelevance: Region-marked edit instructions are a reusable UI primitive for any image-editing surface in Verevon.
notes: Launched 2025-12-22.

name: Video generation and Video Editor (Studio)
what: Prompt-to-video with scene planning; in 2.0 a timeline Video Editor (desktop Studio) with separate layers for shots, images, captions, motion graphics, voiceover, music, SFX; users edit by hand or ask Manus for another pass; 'Alchemy' mode where Manus directs video+code generation.
how: Models: Seedance 2.5/2.0/2.0 Fast, MiniMax H3 (editor); Veo 3.1 Standard (canvas). Motion graphics generated as code (Python/FFmpeg). Web users are pushed to the desktop app to edit. 16:9 output listed as 1080x720 (likely doc error).
verevonRelevance: Shows the pattern 'agent produces an editable project, not a flat export' which Verevon should adopt for every artifact type.
notes: Manus itself says 2.0 'still has quite a few rough edges'.

name: Game Dev (templates, tweak panel, multiplayer)
what: Start from playable templates (scrolling, jumping, block puzzle), Edit/Tweak panel exposes live parameters (speed, gravity, spawn rate), assets management with AI editing, publish as a website; multiplayer requires buying a Cloud Computer which Manus provisions for server/networking/state sync.
how: Studio add-on using video, image and coding models incl. Max Ultra; Configure > Multiplayer > Select Cloud Computer > Buy.
verevonRelevance: Low direct relevance; the generated 'tweak panel' of live parameters is a transferable idea for any generated app.

name: Image generation and AI music generator
what: Standalone AI image generator and AI music generator product pages; GPT Image 2 added for slides; music generator shipped in mobile 26.6.x.
how: Marketing pages /ai-image-generator, /ai-music-generator; models not fully named for music.
verevonRelevance: Table-stakes multimodal generation behind one chat.
notes: Marketing-level evidence for music.

name: Meeting Minutes (on-device recording + transcription)
what: One-tap recording of in-person meetings with live auto-transcription, speaker recognition, structured summary with attendees and to-dos; works offline mid-recording; recording free, analysis costs credits.
how: Desktop (macOS, Windows) and mobile apps; notes become context for follow-on deliverables in the same task; attendees can be invited to the task.
verevonRelevance: Audio capture that flows straight into an agent task is a natural Verevon mobile feature.
notes: Launched 2026-01-12; not for online meetings (Zoom connector covers those).

name: Voice input across surfaces
what: Voice messages are transcribed in Telegram/Slack/LINE agents, mobile Design View and Remote Control; API accepts 'voice' content parts that are transcribed.
how: task.create ContentPart type 'voice' (file_id/url/base64); channel bots auto-transcribe.
verevonRelevance: STT as a first-class message part type in Model Plane.
notes: No realtime voice conversation (TTS back-and-forth) is documented.

name: ElevenLabs connector (TTS, voice clone, SFX, transcription)
what: Generate multilingual speech/voiceovers, clone voices, design sound effects, transcribe with speaker labels, build voice apps, from one chat.
how: OAuth connector to the user's ElevenLabs account; billing stays with ElevenLabs; outputs returned into the Manus session.
verevonRelevance: Pattern: outsource audio to a BYO-account provider rather than own the model.

name: File upload and attachments (large files)
what: Users upload images, PDFs, docs, spreadsheets, audio, video; API supports files up to 512 MB via presigned upload, 20 MB via URL or base64; files auto-expire after 48h unless used.
how: file.upload returns presigned URL; file.detail/delete; attachments resolved as ContentParts; website references resolved per Attachments doc.
verevonRelevance: Presigned direct upload + short TTL is a good Data Plane/Model Plane boundary.

name: Spreadsheet and data analysis work
what: Manus 1.6 highlighted financial modeling and automated reports; spreadsheets are an artifact type; PPT charts are backed by embedded data tables.
how: Sandbox code execution (Python) produces xlsx/csv; artifact type 'spreadsheets'.
verevonRelevance: Data analysis via sandbox code is standard; Verevon's sandboxes should return typed artifacts.

name: Documents export (PDF/DOCX from Markdown)
what: Markdown outputs can be delivered as PDF or Word; slides as pptx; chat channels convert presentations and markdown to PDF for delivery.
how: task.listMessages slides_format=pptx, markdown_format=pdf|docx; Slack/LINE bots auto-convert.
verevonRelevance: Export formats as a parameter of the message-listing API is a neat approach.

name: Wide Research (parallel sub-agents)
what: Complex research is split into independent sub-tasks, each run by a full Manus instance in its own VM with a fresh context window; controller synthesizes; help center cites 20 concurrent subtasks and a 50-credit cap per subtask; marketing cites hundreds of items.
how: Controller decomposes considering dependencies; sub-agents do not talk to each other; results merged by controller using its unused context; auto-triggered (no manual toggle per help); Max architecture for sub-agents since 1.6; paid plans only.
verevonRelevance: A map-reduce run topology (controller + isolated subruns with per-subrun budget cap) belongs in Model Plane's run model.
notes: Marketing ('100x compute per user') vs documented limits (20 concurrent) differ; the per-subtask credit cap is a good budget-control pattern.

name: Cloud Browser (sandbox browser with live view and take-over)
what: Default browsing happens in a sandboxed cloud browser the user can watch in real time; when a CAPTCHA/SMS/MFA appears the user gets a notification, takes over, completes it and hands control back; users can pre-login to accounts and manage/clear logged-in sessions.
how: Settings > Cloud Browser > Take Over Notifications; Logged-in Accounts panel; data-center IPs so some sites challenge more; passwords not stored.
verevonRelevance: Directly comparable to Quarry-v2 browser execution; the human take-over handshake with notification is the piece to copy.

name: Browser Operator / My Browser (local browser extension)
what: Chrome/Edge extension lets Manus act in the user's real browser with existing logins and local IP; per-task one-time Authorize; opens a tab group named after the task; user can watch, take over by clicking in, or stop by closing the tab; every action logged; Preferred Browser selection.
how: 'My Browser' connector; API event needConnectMyBrowser + browser.onlineList + confirmAction select client_id; desktop must be online but tasks can be started from phone; beta, drag-and-drop/multi-step forms imperfect.
verevonRelevance: Matches Verevon's 'Model proposes, Quarry executes or rejects' with a user-held local browser as a grant target; the per-task grant + audit trail are the governance primitives.

name: Connectors (OAuth app integrations, ~70)
what: OAuth-based connectors (Gmail, Google Calendar/Drive, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Stripe, HubSpot, Airtable, Zoom, Shopify, Canva, Mobbin, Supabase, Meta Ads, Instagram, Similarweb, Higgsfield, ElevenLabs, ...) usable in tasks, projects and schedules; custom MCP/API connectors.
how: Authorize in web app; API passes connector UUIDs; resolution explicit > project default > user default; clear_connectors on follow-ups; uninstalled connectors silently skipped; revocable from integrations page.
verevonRelevance: Equivalent to integration-corev2 provider actions; the three-level default resolution is worth copying.

name: Recommended connectors in-conversation
what: When a task needs an app that is not connected, Manus recommends the connector inline; user reviews and approves without leaving the chat; Manus never bypasses login/authorization.
how: Matching against the user's connector catalog descriptions vs task; enablement card in chat; OAuth still user-completed.
verevonRelevance: Just-in-time integration prompts reduce setup friction; fits Verevon's grant model.

name: Multi-account connectors (Gmail/Calendar)
what: Multiple Gmail/Calendar accounts can be connected; Manus picks accounts by task context, and the user chooses the sending account for final actions.
how: Accounts assignable per task, Project, or schedule; docs advise naming the account explicitly.
verevonRelevance: Identity-per-connector-instance is needed for Verevon enterprise users with several mailboxes.

name: Built-in data integrations (Similarweb) wrapped as skills
what: Third-party data sources like Similarweb are available natively as data integrations/skills (traffic, keywords, referrals), billed in credits.
how: Data Integrations docs; 'skill library' wraps Similarweb as a Skill.
verevonRelevance: Bundled paid data sources inside credits is a monetization pattern.

name: Web search in Chat mode
what: Chat mode can run online searches and accept images/PDFs/text.
how: Not detailed; part of Chat mode capabilities.
verevonRelevance: Baseline.
notes: Citation UI is not documented in public sources; low visibility.

name: Cascade harness (lazy capability loading)
what: Manus 2.0's in-house agent harness starts lean and loads specialist capabilities only when the task needs them, keeping brief, page, video and automation in one project; vendor claims 23.2% fewer tokens, 28.2% faster, 32% cheaper in one configuration.
how: Progressive loading of tools/skills; API event types cascadeAskUser and 'Profile Agent Cascade sub-lane' connector confirmations indicate sub-lanes within a run.
verevonRelevance: Core lesson for Model Plane: keep tool definitions stable for caching but expose capabilities progressively (skills metadata first).
notes: Benchmarks are vendor self-reported, single configuration.

name: Plan Mode (review-before-execute)
what: Manual mode where Manus runs a feasibility check, asks clarifying questions if needed, and presents a structured Markdown plan (goals, steps, constraints); nothing runs until the user confirms; plan is editable by hand or via Manus, before and after confirmation.
how: '/Plan' in web, '+' > Plan Mode on mobile; plan becomes the reference document for execution; combinable with Branch and version rollback.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agent page needs a plan artifact that is a first-class, editable run input.

name: Agent asks questions / interactive mode
what: Agent can pause to ask the user questions with optional choice lists (single/multiple select) or free text; API interactive_mode toggles whether the agent may pause.
how: Events messageAskUser/cascadeAskUser with question_expectation {options, selection_mode, response_method=send_message}; answered via task.sendMessage.
verevonRelevance: Structured question events (options + selection mode) are a clean protocol element for Verevon's run event stream.

name: Action confirmations with typed input schemas
what: Sensitive actions (send email, deploy, terminal execute, calendar delete, Meta marketing, video premium choice, secrets request) pause the task with a confirmation whose input shape is given by a schema.
how: status waiting + waiting_for_event_type/id + confirm_input_schema; task.confirmAction; some types ignore accept:false; some confirmations only in UI (connector CRUD, self-config save, Agent config cards).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's browser grants and provider actions should expose typed confirmation events exactly like this.
notes: 'Skip confirmations' toggle exists for trusted scheduled workflows.

name: Task lifecycle statuses and background jobs
what: Tasks run asynchronously with statuses running/stopped/waiting/error; 'stopped' can still have background jobs; tasks can be stopped and later resumed by a message, schedule or trigger.
how: status_update events; task.detail.has_running_background_jobs tri-state (true/false/omitted=unknown); task.stop; stop_reason finish|ask.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane sessions/runs: adopt explicit tri-state background-job signalling and resumable stopped runs.

name: Scheduled Tasks 2.0 (same-context recurring runs)
what: Recurring runs can continue inside the same task (reusing instructions, files, history, past results) or spawn separate tasks; side panel with schedule and calendar views; run cards link to outputs; settings for skip confirmations, connectors, agent choice, Project config, cloud computer.
how: Time-based triggers; apps built with Manus can own scheduled actions; Free plan 2 scheduled automations, Pro 20.
verevonRelevance: Same-context recurrence (state accumulates in one session) is a distinct design worth evaluating against Verevon's run model.
notes: 2026-05-18; superseded/extended by Automations in 2.0.

name: Automations (event-triggered workflows)
what: Manus 2.0 replaces Scheduled Tasks with Automations: triggers from new email, Slack message, calendar event, Notion update, ad-performance change; one prompt describes trigger and task; Create menu offers Schedule, Triggered task, Advanced automation (Beta).
how: Event subscriptions through connectors; permanent automations may require a Cloud Computer.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can mirror this using Ingestion Plane events as triggers for Model Plane runs.
notes: Advanced automation still Beta.

name: Context engineering practices (KV-cache, masking, file-as-memory, todo recitation, keep errors)
what: Published engineering lessons: stable prompt prefix and append-only context for KV-cache hits; mask tool logits instead of removing tools; filesystem as restorable external memory; rewrite todo.md to keep goals in recent attention; keep failed actions in context; add controlled diversity to avoid few-shot ruts.
how: State machine chooses allowed tools via logit masking with prefixed tool names (browser_, shell_); three function-calling prefill modes (Auto/Required/Specified); ~50 tool calls per typical task; 100:1 input:output tokens.
verevonRelevance: These are directly actionable Model Plane rules (prompt caching, deterministic serialization, tool masking, compaction by reference).
notes: 2025-07-18; best public write-up of harness internals from any vendor.

name: Error recovery via automatic sandbox replacement
what: After an unrecoverable sandbox error Manus replaces the sandbox so the task can continue; failed tasks due to Manus-side issues are refunded.
how: Sandbox lifecycle manager; refund policy in billing docs.
verevonRelevance: Sandbox re-provisioning plus credit refund is a user-trust mechanism.

name: Agent profiles / effort levels
what: Agent profile per task: standard, lite, max, max-medium, max-high, max-extra, max-ultra; free accounts downgraded to lite; Max Ultra used for Game Dev quality.
how: task.create agent_profile; versioned aliases accepted but version ignored.
verevonRelevance: A single 'effort ladder' parameter abstracting model+reasoning is cleaner than exposing raw model pickers.
notes: Overlaps category 9.

name: Structured output extraction
what: API callers supply a JSON Schema; after the run finishes a separate extraction step produces a conforming value with success/error flags; schema is armed across ask-pauses and consumed on finish.
how: structured_output_schema (strict subset: root object, additionalProperties false, all required, depth 5, no allOf/oneOf); result event structured_output_result or webhook task_stopped.
verevonRelevance: Post-hoc extraction (not constraining the agent) is a pragmatic approach for Verevon's app-server API.

name: Custom Agents with persistent main thread and subtasks
what: Each account has a default IM agent and can have custom agents (incl. Cue agents) with nickname/description; each agent has a persistent main task (conversation thread) and spawns agent_subtask tasks.
how: agent.list/detail/update; task_type agent_subtask; shortcuts agent-default-main_task.
verevonRelevance: Persistent agent thread + child runs is a model for Verevon 'agents' page entities.

name: Webhooks for task lifecycle
what: task_created, task_stopped (finish|ask, attachments, structured_output), task_deleted events delivered to HTTPS endpoints; one webhook per Open App.
how: webhook.create/list/delete/publicKey; endpoint must answer 200 within 10 s and pass a test request; signature verification documented separately.
verevonRelevance: Baseline for Verevon app-server.

name: Parallel tasks and concurrency limits
what: Each task has its own VM so tasks run in parallel; Free: 1 concurrent task, Pro: 20 concurrent tasks.
how: Per-plan concurrency caps.
verevonRelevance: Concurrency as a plan dimension in Control Plane billing.

name: Agent Skills (SKILL.md open standard) with progressive disclosure
what: Skills are folders with SKILL.md plus scripts/references/templates; metadata (~100 tokens) loads at start, instructions (<5k tokens) on trigger, resources on demand; invoked automatically or via /SKILL_NAME.
how: Agent reads skill dir in Ubuntu sandbox, parses SKILL.md, runs bundled scripts; adopted Anthropic's Agent Skills standard (2026-01-27).
verevonRelevance: Verevon should adopt the same SKILL.md format for portability with Claude/Codex ecosystems.

name: Build a Skill with Manus (auto-packaging workflows)
what: Ask Manus to 'package this workflow as a Skill'; it analyzes the interaction, writes SKILL.md, bundles scripts and offers a .skill download.
how: Skill card with Download; .skill/.zip/folder upload; GitHub public repo import; Manus can review imported skills for risk.
verevonRelevance: Procedure learning loop (Hermes-like) with a user-visible artifact; Verevon could do this at session end.

name: Project Skills, Team Skill Library, lock
what: Each project has a curated skill library drawn from My Skills, Team Skills, Official Essential/Pro skills; only skills in the library can trigger in that project; lock icon prevents members editing.
how: Project > Skills > + Add; filter Team/My Skills; API project.update skills, skill.list; enable_skills/force_skills on task.create.
verevonRelevance: Scoping which skills may fire per workspace is a governance feature Verevon orgs will want.

name: Custom MCP and API connectors
what: Users can create/update custom MCP and API connectors (from chat on mobile 26.11.x); MCP connectors such as HubSpot, Notion, Higgsfield, Supabase have setup guides.
how: Connector framework supports MCP servers and custom APIs; Skills vs MCP positioning: MCP for data access, Skills for workflows.
verevonRelevance: MCP support is table stakes; creation from chat is a nice UX.

name: Public API v2 (tasks, projects, skills, agents, files, artifacts, websites, usage)
what: Full REST API with OpenAPI spec, per-user rate limits (task.create 10/min), API keys or OAuth2, OpenAI-SDK compatibility in v1 (deprecated).
how: api.manus.ai/v2/*.* RPC-style endpoints; cursor pagination; usage.* endpoints for credits and team logs.
verevonRelevance: Reference shape for Verevon's app-server/SDK; note the RPC naming and the usage endpoints.

name: Open Apps (OAuth2 client types and scopes)
what: Team accounts can register OAuth apps: standard team (scoped), trusted_team (full access, admin-created), trusted_public (partners; hidden context). Scopes: create_task, manage_all_tasks, create_project, use_connectors, use_my_browsers; apps can bundle up to 50 private skills.
how: PKCE+secret; 24h access/30d refresh tokens; 5 rotating secrets; one webhook per app; token invalidation on scope expansion.
verevonRelevance: Control Plane identity: good template for third-party app authorization in Verevon.

name: Hidden application context
what: Trusted public clients can send text parts the agent sees but users do not, preserving position relative to visible text; affects behavior and skill selection; readable only by the same client with verbose listing.
how: ContentPart visibility: hidden; counts toward token limit; files/voice cannot be hidden.
verevonRelevance: Verevon embedding partners may need system-side context injection with audit; copy the permission gating.
notes: Potential prompt-injection vector if misused; gated to partners.

name: Manus API skill for coding agents
what: An installable skill (npx skills add https://open.manus.ai/docs) teaches Codex and compatible agents to integrate the API; inside Manus, /manus-api does the same.
how: Skill reads live docs for schemas; no credentials embedded.
verevonRelevance: Publish a Verevon API skill in the same format to make Verevon easy to integrate from other agents.

name: Manus Flex (bring your own inference provider)
what: Users connect their own API key from OpenRouter, Fireworks or Modal, choose a primary model and reasoning-effort level, and run Manus' harness on it; provider bills inference, Manus credits still cover other services.
how: Flex Inference Partner Program; works with existing projects/tools/workflows.
verevonRelevance: BYO-key routing with per-run effort control is a Model Plane feature Verevon could offer to enterprise tenants.
notes: 2026-09-29; overlaps category 9.

name: Mail Manus (email as a task channel)
what: Each account gets a Manus email address; approved senders (<=10) create tasks by email or forwarding; Workflow Emails carry custom instructions (Free 3, paid 30); cc'd people join the task.
how: Settings > Mail Manus; custom address changeable every 7 days.
verevonRelevance: Email-ingress to runs is cheap to build on Verevon's Ingestion Plane and valuable for ops users.

name: Messaging-channel agents (Telegram, Slack, LINE)
what: Manus Agents live in Telegram, Slack (DM agent, @mention in threads, MCP connector) and LINE; accept text, voice, images, video, files; deliver PDFs/media/preview links; Slack slash commands (/new_task, /new_schedule, /agent_mode ...).
how: Agents tab > Connect > QR/link; DM tasks appear under Agents not Past Tasks; presentations converted to PDF; plain-text replies.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Channel Plane is docs-only/future; Manus shows the minimal viable channel surface (ingest, deliver converted files, persistent DM memory).

name: Per-task cloud sandbox VM (Ubuntu) with sleep/wake and recycling
what: Every task gets an isolated cloud VM with network, filesystem, browser, tools and root; sleeps when idle, wakes on demand; recycled after 7 days (Free) / 21 days (Pro) of sleep; artifacts/attachments/Slides/WebDev files restored, temp files not.
how: Zero-trust isolation; session/account data unreachable from sandbox; 'View all files in this task'; Manus can zip and deliver files.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane sandboxes: adopt explicit sleep/recycle tiers and a restore-set contract.
notes: VM specs not published; performance 'not fixed'.

name: Take over VS Code / browser inside sandbox
what: Users can take control of the sandbox's browser or VS Code from within the task when Manus asks for help or on their own initiative.
how: Help article with screenshots; troubleshooting articles for VS Code not working.
verevonRelevance: Human-in-the-loop handoff to the same environment the agent uses (shared VM) is a strong transparency feature.

name: My Computer (local desktop control via Manus Desktop)
what: Desktop app lets Manus run terminal commands, read/edit files in authorized folders, launch local apps, use local Python/Node/Swift/Xcode and GPU; tasks can be assigned remotely from a phone while the desktop runs.
how: Folder-scoped authorization; command approval Allow Once / Always Allow (blog) or only for sensitive commands with scope 'current task'/'current path' (help); works with Projects, Agents, Scheduled Tasks; command-line, not GUI automation.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's 'remote devices' story: a thin local agent with folder grants and typed command approvals.
notes: Blog and help differ on approval granularity; launched 2026-03-16.

name: Remote Control and Computer Use (2.0)
what: From a phone, give voice/text commands and watch the desktop live; Manus works in a visible, separate workspace with approved files, browser and apps; instructions can be changed mid-task.
how: Authorized desktop session streamed to mobile; builds on Manus Studio.
verevonRelevance: Mobile-as-remote for a desktop agent; relevant if Verevon ships a desktop companion.
notes: Marketing-level detail only.

name: Cloud Computer (persistent always-on VM add-on)
what: Purchasable dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 VM with public IP: Standard $30/mo (2 vCPU, 4 GB, 70 GB), Advanced $50/mo (2 vCPU, 8 GB, 120 GB); persists files/tools/DBs; SSH or web terminal; CPU/mem/storage dashboard; deleted if subscription lapses.
how: Settings > My Computer > Create Cloud Computer; Manus assigns it per task when continuous uptime is needed; access permission follows last message sender in session.
verevonRelevance: Clear separation of ephemeral sandbox vs paid persistent machine is a billing and architecture model Verevon could reuse.
notes: CLI only, no desktop GUI.

name: Full-stack Web Builder with integrated testing browser
